title: Oscar and the Safehouse
premise: August Thornbury, a disgraced intelligence analyst scraping by on unattributable contract work, is hired to investigate why every digital trace of Flight 4471 evaporated while the plane was still airborne. The trail leads to a decommissioned safehouse network their late father helped build, now repurposed by a cabal staging a catastrophic 'accident' to bury an inheritance of secrets. August must reconcile the father they resented with the system he left behind, racing to expose the plot before a second flight vanishes for real. In the end, August burns their own last shred of anonymity to force the truth into daylight, surviving at the cost of the belonging they'd finally begun to find.
about_author: Ansel Brightwater spent a decade in logistics before turning to fiction, writing in the margins of night shifts and layovers. They live near a regional airport and claim the best plots arrive at cruising altitude.

chapters.title: The Client Without a Name
chapters.summary: August's POV. Broke and blacklisted, August takes a cash job from a broker who won't say who's paying: find out who erased Flight 4471 from every database mid-flight. The emotional beat is weary cynicism masking hunger for one meaningful case.

chapters.title: Ghosts at Altitude
chapters.summary: August interviews air traffic staff who swear the plane landed, though no record exists. A controller slips them a fragment of raw radar data. Beat: first crack of dread — this wasn't a glitch, it was surgery.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Home
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter as August works the radar fragment, recalling the three careers that ended in disgrace. Beat: self-loathing sharpened into resolve; August realizes the erasure used tradecraft only insiders would know.

chapters.title: The Broker's Warning
chapters.summary: The broker warns August off, terrified, then disappears. August finds the payment traced to a shell company linked to a defunct government program: Safehouse. Beat: isolation deepening into paranoia.

chapters.title: What Father Built
chapters.summary: August digs into family archives and discovers their estranged father co-designed the Safehouse network — bunkers that could make things unexist. Beat: grief and fury colliding; the case just became personal inheritance.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest, Missing
chapters.summary: August tracks down a manifest survivor's widow, who reveals her husband was a Safehouse auditor about to testify. Beat: cold clarity — the vanished flight was a murder weapon.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Looking
chapters.summary: A rival investigator, Mara Voss, corners August; she's been hired by insurers. Uneasy alliance forms over shared evidence. Beat: reluctant warmth, the first belonging August has felt in years.

chapters.title: The Second List
chapters.summary: Voss shares her client's list: five more people tied to Safehouse are booked on upcoming flights. One departs in nine days. Beat: ticking clock installed; dread becomes urgency.

chapters.title: Safehouse Nine
chapters.summary: August breaks into a derelict Safehouse site and finds it freshly powered, servers humming, running the erasure software. Beat: awe curdling into horror at how alive the inheritance is.

chapters.title: Ambush in the Dark
chapters.summary: Attackers hit the site; August and Voss escape separately, Voss wounded. August goes dark using father's old protocols. Beat: fear transformed into grim competence — the legacy protects them.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: August locates Aldous Reeve, the program's living architect, hiding in plain sight. Reeve admits the cabal revived his work but claims innocence. Beat: moral vertigo — the mentor figure may be victim or spider.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Eight Left
chapters.summary: August decodes Safehouse ledgers: the target flight carries a whistleblower holding proof of the cabal's funding. Beat: stakes crystallize — save one person or expose everything, maybe not both.

chapters.title: Trusted Hands
chapters.summary: August brings in an old colleague, Dev, the only person who never abandoned them. Dev hesitates, then commits. Beat: fragile trust rebuilt; August dares to hope again.

chapters.title: Reeve's Confession
chapters.summary: Reeve reveals the cabal's leader is inside the oversight agency that once fired August. He gives them a backdoor key, then is found dead hours later. Beat: betrayal and loss hardening August's purpose.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: August is framed for Reeve's murder; Dev's contact burns them, forcing Dev to choose sides. Voss goes underground with August. Beat: everything stripped away except the two of them and the truth.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Terminal
chapters.summary: Two days out. August infiltrates the airport's data center to plant a tripwire that will preserve records no matter what. Nearly caught. Beat: claustrophobic tension, competence under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Bought
chapters.summary: Voss traces the money to a private foundation buying silence across three governments. The scale stuns them. Beat: despair at the machinery — then defiance.

chapters.title: Boarding
chapters.summary: Day of the flight. August and Voss identify the whistleblower, Ilsa Brandt, mid-terminal, pursued by a cleaner team. Beat: breathless pursuit, the clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: The cabal triggers the erasure early; systems cascade offline, the plane radio-silent on screens. August uses the backdoor key to hold one thread of data alive. Beat: climax begins — a knife fight inside the machine.

chapters.title: The Landing That Couldn't Be Erased
chapters.summary: August forces the preserved feed public through every channel at once, including the agency that ruined them. The plane lands safely; Brandt walks out with the ledger. Beat: triumphant, costly exposure.

chapters.title: Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Fallout: hearings, arrests, and August's name dragged through both infamy and vindication. Dev returns, chastened; Voss offers partnership. Beat: bittersweet accounting of what survival cost.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: August visits their father's grave, finally understanding what he built and what he feared. They keep the Safehouse keys — not to hide, but to guard. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging chosen, not granted.
